title: Thakur and Siraj Bowl New Zealand Out for 185 as Kohli Seals Series
excerpt: India won the second ODI in Christchurch by five wickets, chasing 186 in 32 overs behind Virat Kohli's 92, to lead the series 2-0.
body:
• India bowled New Zealand out for 185 in 46.1 overs in the second ODI at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, with Shardul Thakur taking 4 for 27 and Mohammed Siraj 3 for 30.
  • Virat Kohli's 92 off 83 balls led the chase as India reached 191 for 5 in 32 overs to win by five wickets.
  • Mitchell Santner's 65 off 44 balls was the only substantial resistance after New Zealand collapsed to 94 for 6.
  • India lead the three-match series 2-0; the final ODI is in Wellington on Sunday, November 8.

India's seamers bowled New Zealand out for 185 and Virat Kohli finished the job with 92, as India won the second ODI at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, by five wickets on Thursday to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. India reached 191 for 5 in just 32 overs, closing out a match that was effectively decided in a first session played, as the Indian Express put it, like a Test match from another era.

A collapse in two acts

Asked to bat on a surface offering swing, seam and uneven bounce, New Zealand never recovered from a slow, grinding start. Devon Conway took 52 balls for his 25, Daryl Mitchell 34 balls for 23, and at 94 for 6 in the 27th over the innings was going nowhere. Shardul Thakur, only recalled recently and playing because Arshdeep Singh was rested, was the main destroyer with 4 for 27; Mohammed Siraj took 3 for 30, and Kuldeep Yadav 2 for 35.

The one passage that broke the pattern came from Mitchell Santner, who attacked for 65 off 44 balls with six fours and three sixes. Michael Bracewell made 40, but Santner's dismissal in the 47th over ended the innings at 185.

"It was a throwback to the 1990s for New Zealand as the Indian seamers tormented them on a surface that offered generous swing, seam movement and uneven bounce."

— The Indian Express

The subplot: Mitchell against Kuldeep

One duel ran through the innings. Daryl Mitchell, New Zealand's best player of spin, managed only six runs off the 16 balls he faced from Kuldeep Yadav, and the pressure told: it was Thakur, not Kuldeep, who dismissed him, caught at deep cover, with Mitchell still short of fluency. Kuldeep finished with two wickets of his own, and New Zealand's middle order never found a release against either discipline.

Kohli closes it out

The chase was a formality paced by Kohli, who made 92 off 83 balls with 11 fours and a six and was named Player of the Match. KL Rahul's unbeaten 36 off 28 balls hurried the finish, and India were home with 18 overs to spare. Kyle Jamieson took 2 for 37 and Jacob Duffy 2 for 31 for New Zealand.

India had won the Auckland opener by five wickets under the DLS method, when Kohli made 74. The series concludes at Wellington on Sunday, November 8, with India playing for a clean sweep and New Zealand for a consolation win. Full scorecard: Cricbuzz.
